proposals.evidence: Platts identifies Hindustani piyāz onion as Persian, and Jambu already attests the regional Hindi pyāj donor. Survey pyāj/pyāz and vocalic or affricated variants fit this widespread loan family. Hindi/Urdu is used as a provisional contact-language proxy rather than claiming direct Persian transmission; Bengali/Oriya or neighbouring Pahari mediation may intervene, and final i is retained as regional adaptation.
